title: A code item's land.end row says lane=content, and ops prints land.end before the last land.step it shares a timestamp with
goal: a land run that waited for a code item's merge request ends with a land.end row that names the code lane; ops prints a landing's land.end row after its last land.step row when the two share a timestamp

run: import sys;t=open('_tools/bl_land.py',encoding='utf-8').read();sys.exit(1 if 'LAND_OPS["lane"] = "code" if late else "content"' in t else 0)

repro_reason: the lane is set in the second pass of a land run, which is reached only after a forge merge request merges; no planted root reaches it offline

run:
import contextlib, io, sys, types
sys.path.insert(0, "_tools")
import bl_ops, bl_stall
# a land.end row and the last land.step row of one landing share a timestamp; the end row has the smaller id
rows = [
    {"id": "a-end-row", "ts": "2026-11-09T01:00:00.000Z", "event": "land.end", "item": "ST-aaaaaaaa", "exit": 0, "ms": 5, "lane": "code"},
    {"id": "z-step-row", "ts": "2026-11-09T01:00:00.000Z", "event": "land.step", "item": "ST-aaaaaaaa", "step": "kbgit.py-sync-push", "exit": 0, "ms": 5},
]
bl_ops.sprint_items = lambda bl, sid: {"ST-aaaaaaaa"}
bl_stall.ops_rows = lambda root: sorted(rows, key=lambda r: (r["ts"], r["id"]))
bl = types.SimpleNamespace(root=".", label=lambda i: i)
out = io.StringIO()
with contextlib.redirect_stdout(out), contextlib.redirect_stderr(out):
    bl_ops.cmd_ops(bl, types.SimpleNamespace(id="SP-aaaaaaaa"))
events = [ln.split()[1] for ln in out.getvalue().splitlines() if "land." in ln]
print("ops prints", events)
sys.exit(0 if events == ["land.step", "land.end"] else 1)

clauses.clause: a land run that waited for a code item's merge request ends with a land.end row that names the code lane
ops prints a landing's land.end row after its last land.step row when the two share a timestamp

notes: Seen again at SP-ia6xayiy close (2026-10-14): backlog.py ops SP-ia6xayiy prints lane=content on the land.end rows of BG-ms5dtnnr, BG-zwf3rs5y, BG-ph7dcjhz, ST-2ietdnca, ST-ns63tfx5, ST-fla2es24 and ST-ruxcexsg, each of which pushed code/<id> and waited for its merge request; the land.end rows of BG-ph7dcjhz, ST-ns63tfx5 and ST-ruxcexsg print before their last kbgit.py-sync-push step row. Premise run 2026-11-09 on the base: bl_land.py still sets LAND_OPS lane per pass (the repro fails on it), and the night's ops rows (2026-11-08 18:00 to 2026-11-09 13:00 CET) hold 129 code items whose first pass ended lane=code and whose last pass ended lane=content (155 of 158 items end at lane=content). The ordering check plants a land.end and a land.step row of one timestamp (the end row with the smaller id) through bl_ops.cmd_ops; on the base ops prints land.end first, so the fix sorts in bl_ops (bl_stall.ops_rows is not in the touches). The lane clause's repro reads source text, since the lane is set in the second pass of a run that needs a forge merge request (repro_reason); after BG-ot47avdg the one land run reaches that pass in one go, so a code landing's land.end for the whole run is the row to read.
